finding_1_no_implementation.claim: Agent-Ready has no implementation module, no JSON schema and no CLI in this repository.
finding_1_no_implementation.method: grep for agent-ready/agent_ready across src/ test/ tests/ tools/ scripts/; search for any *assessment*.schema.json
code_references_found: tools/evidence/reconcile_wave1.py (reads assessments; does not produce them)
finding_1_no_implementation.note: src/domain/rai.mjs is a different concept: its DISPOSITIONS are RESOLVED/REJECTED/SUPERSEDED, which are finding dispositions, not readiness dispositions.
finding_1_no_implementation.consequence: Phase 4's stated input 'actual Agent-Ready implementation/schema/CLI' does not exist. The matrix must be derived from governing authority and retained artifacts, and the absence is itself the phase's primary gap.

finding_2_schema_drift.claim: 32 assessment files carry two incompatible shapes; no field is present in all 32.

correction.what_was_wrong: The prework reported disposition 'absent' in 17 of 32 files. That was a top-level-only reading. All 17 MCP envelopes carry isError=false and READY nested in structuredContent, matching their parsed text payload. Normalized, the observed count is READY=31, not 14.
correction.what_stands: The two incompatible serialization shapes are real, and no top-level field is common to all 32. The drift finding holds; the absence count did not.

finding_3_non_ready_not_persisted.status: CORRECTED — the original claim was false
finding_3_non_ready_not_persisted.corrected_by: codex/gpt-6-astra during POSTW1-AGENTREADY-004, disputed rather than accepted
finding_3_non_ready_not_persisted.original_claim: BLOCKED and SPLIT_RECOMMENDED never appear as a persisted disposition in any assessment file, although Wave 1 produced both.
finding_3_non_ready_not_persisted.why_it_was_wrong: The claim was derived from the working-tree snapshot only. A working tree is not the persistence layer. Git history retains the full verdict sequence for docs/work-units/python/PY-10.assessment.json: c32830b BLOCKED -> 1f16b81 SPLIT_RECOMMENDED -> 693fef9 READY, each with a descriptive commit message naming the reassessment.
finding_3_non_ready_not_persisted.verified_by: git log --follow plus git show of the disposition field at each revision
finding_3_non_ready_not_persisted.corrected_claim: Non-READY dispositions persist in Git history. What differs between BIUs is working-tree retention: PY-09B kept a dated sibling file, PY-10 did not. That is a retention convention inconsistency, not silent coercion.
finding_3_non_ready_not_persisted.consequence_had_it_stood: Phase 4 would have reported silent coercion that the evidence disproves. The dispatched session disputed the premise instead of adopting it.

finding_4_lrn008_mischaracterised_in_dis.status: CORRECTED — the dispatch prompt was wrong
finding_4_lrn008_mischaracterised_in_dis.claim_in_prompt: conflating execution failures with dispositions 'is the failure LRN-008 records'
finding_4_lrn008_mischaracterised_in_dis.why_it_was_wrong: LRN-008 records a verifier that exited success with no B-DISP verdict and became DURABLE_RESULT_MISSING rather than ACCEPT. The ledger calls it 'a real adverse-input refusal'. It is an instance of the control working, not of coercion occurring.

director_self_assessment.note: Three claims in this prework were wrong, and all three failed the same way: a surface reading treated as a complete one. Non-READY verdicts were called unpersisted because the working tree lacked them (Git had them); dispositions were called absent because the top level lacked them (the envelopes had them); LRN-008 was cited as an instance of coercion when the ledger calls it a refusal that worked. The dispatched session disputed all three rather than inheriting them. Deterministic prework is only as good as the layer it reads, and a prework artifact that feeds a false premise into a phase is more dangerous than no prework, because it arrives labelled deterministic.
